title.narrative: Sustainable Waste Management in Mozambique – Laying the Foundations for a Circular Economy

description.narrative: The number of people residing in urban areas in Mozambique has increased from 3.3 million in 1990 to over 10 million in 2017. This led to a growth of generated waste volumes. Over 98% of the collected waste continues to be disposed at uncontrolled dumpsites, leading to the GHG emissions of 1.5 Mt CO2 per year, frequent uncontrolled fires and continuous health threats to the people living in surrounding areas. The main objective of the project is to improve waste management practices in Mozambique and lay the foundations for the development of a circular economy. The project will be co-financed by the Government of Mozambique up to an amount of EUR 9 million. During the implementation period, the project plans to achieve direct and indirect emission reductions totalling at ca. 143,000 88,073 tCO2e
